## Our industry connections {#industry}

UTSC Management's co-op relationships give us a foundation for bringing industry further into the classroom. Its co-op model includes 12 months of paid work experience within a four-year undergraduate degree. [Management co-op overview](https://utsc.utoronto.ca/mgmt/why-co-op)

```{=html}
<figure class="reading-photo"><button class="photo-button" data-photo="ibm" aria-label="Enlarge the MGOC15 photographs" aria-haspopup="dialog"><img src="assets/images/mgoc15-ibm.png" alt="MGOC15 students and IBM Canada practitioners in teaching sessions, a computer lab and at IBM Canada."></button><figcaption>MGOC15 with IBM Canada. Photograph supplied in the October 2026 MAB presentation.</figcaption></figure>
```

### MGOC15 with IBM Canada

The MAB materials describe Business Data Analytics as co-developed and co-taught by Andre Cire with IBM leaders Manav Gupta and Sadi Khan, including learning on campus and inside IBM Canada. The photographs include a session on retrieval-augmented generation evaluation and AI governance.

The course is an existing example of collaboration. The proposed certificate would explore whether that kind of engagement could extend across a coherent sequence of courses. Partner commitments to the certificate remain under discussion.

### Reimagining recruitment

We could show prospective students what learning with industry would actually involve. A sample class or student demonstration can connect the recruitment message to a concrete course experience.

<details class="reading-disclosure"><summary>A practitioner-led sample class</summary><p>At an applicant event, a practitioner and faculty member could introduce a business challenge and discuss how students would investigate it during a course.</p></details>

<details class="reading-disclosure"><summary>Student work that applicants can inspect</summary><p>With permission, show a project and explain how the student tested its results, responded to feedback and documented its limitations. This is an illustrative recruitment activity, not a claim of measured enrollment gains.</p></details>

<details class="reading-disclosure"><summary>A visible path through the degree</summary><p>Explain where AI learning, practitioner interaction and assessed project work would fit. Any pathway needs to account for prerequisites and the timing of full-time co-op work terms.</p></details>

Co-op jobs remain subject to the normal application and recruitment process. [Management student FAQ](https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/mgmt/student-faq)

## AI certificate concept {#certificate}

A proposed **6–8 month pathway for Management students**, with courses developed and taught alongside industry. The duration comes from the MAB concept notes. Academic requirements and participation are still under discussion.

The common foundation would cover business problem definition, data literacy, model evaluation and responsible AI. Students would need suitable technical preparation, with a preparation route for those with limited programming experience.

### Illustrative course areas

The combinations below are examples for discussion: Google Agentic AI with Gemini, Microsoft agents and automation, and SAS analytics and decisions. Existing IBM participation in MGOC15 does not establish a commitment to this certificate. Google, Microsoft and SAS are prospective examples, not confirmed certificate partners.

{{< include _includes/course-details.qmd >}}

### Learning across technologies

Students would compare approaches and explain their choices, reusing ideas across the course areas. A shared project would connect the courses to a business problem. It would not require combining every vendor's products.

Faculty would determine academic learning outcomes and grades, with practitioner feedback contributing to student work. Assessment could consider problem formulation, testing, responsible use and communication to a business audience.

### Decisions still to make

The credential name and issuing unit, credit status, prerequisites, number of courses, workload and timing need further design. So do faculty capacity, technology access and a sustainable commitment from partners. An academic certificate and a vendor certification would be separate credentials with their own requirements. Course participation would not imply a guaranteed job.

## Advice from the board

Would this pathway help attract Management students and prepare graduates you would want to hire?

What capability would you most want students to demonstrate? Where could partners make the most useful contribution to teaching and feedback?

This webpage supports exploration and discussion. It does not collect responses or present shared polling results.

## Sources and scope {#sources}

Each program entry links to its official institutional source. Research was checked on **October 12, 2026**. Offerings, requirements and delivery arrangements can change. Consult the institution's current catalog for enrollment decisions.

- UTSC Management co-op: [program overview](https://utsc.utoronto.ca/mgmt/why-co-op) and [student FAQ](https://www.utsc.utoronto.ca/mgmt/student-faq).
- MGOC15 course example and the initial certificate concept: departmental **MAB October 2026 draft**, slides 13–14 and associated speaker notes. The full departmental deck is not reproduced here.
- Additional context for the U of T continuing education listings: [School of Continuing Studies overview](https://learn.utoronto.ca/curiousu-blog/curiosity/how-scs-integrating-ai-lifelong-learning). Current course counts, prices and schedules are not asserted here.
- A broader list of recognized master's offerings is available from the [Vector Institute](https://vectorinstitute.ai/research-talent/students/ai-masters-programs/).

Industry engagement already exists in several programs. A coherent undergraduate Management pathway with recurring practitioner involvement is a design hypothesis to explore, not a verified claim of uniqueness.
